recipes.name: Demon Burger inspired by Dragon Ball Daima
ingredients: 75 g (5 1/2 tbsp) melted butter, room temperature, more for brushing
150 g riced baked potato (1 cup baked potato before riced)
freshly ground black pepper, to taste
instructions: For the Meat Prep
For the Tongue
Remove the outer membrane by trimming it with a sharp boning knife. Remove any excess gristle or tough pieces from the outside. Refrigerate until ready to use. - ½ lb beef tongue
For the Patties
Prepare rimmed baking sheets with parchment paper.
Cut the chuck roast, pork belly and lamb into 1 inch cubes. - 1 lb chuck roast - ½ lb pork belly - 1 lb lamb shoulder

Place the cubes onto the prepared baking sheets. Freeze for 20-30 minutes, or until the meat is firm to the touch, but not completely frozen through. - 1 lb chuck roast - 1 lb lamb shoulder - ½ lb pork belly

Working in batches, add the beef, pork and lamb to the bowl of a food processor. Process until the meat mixture resembles tiny pebbles, then transfer to a large bowl. Refrigerate the bowl while you are processing the remaining meat. - 1 lb chuck roast - ½ lb pork belly - 1 lb lamb shoulder

Once all of the meat is ground, toss to combine, then add the spices to the ground meat. Gently mix to incorporate the spices. - 2 tsp smoked paprika - 2 tsp ground ginger - 2 tsp mustard powder - 2 tsp white pepper - 2 tsp onion powder - kosher salt to taste - 1 lb chuck roast - 1 lb lamb shoulder - ½ lb pork belly

Divide the meat into 5 patty balls, about ⅓ lb each, and place on a parchment-lined rimmed baking sheet. Refrigerate for at least 1 hour, or until the fat has re-solidified and the meat is chilled. - For the Patties
For the Buns (after Brian Lagerstrom)
Microwaving the potato will give you a squishy consistency for ricing. - 150 g riced baked potato (1 cup baked potato before riced)

In the bowl of a stand mixer, combine warm water, sugar, egg, milk, butter, bloomed yeast, activated charcoal, riced baked potato, all purpose flour, and salt. - 250 g warm water - 100 g sugar - 1 large egg - 75 g (5 1/2 tbsp) melted butter room temperature, more for brushing - 8 g (2 1/2 tsp) instant yeast bloomed - 3 tbsp activated charcoal - 150 g riced baked potato (1 cup baked potato before riced) - 625 g (5 cups) all purpose flour - 2 tsp kosher salt
Mix with a dough hook on medium speed for 15-20 minutes. - For the Activated Charcoal Buns

The activated charcoal will absorb moisture, so add water as needed and scrape down the sides of the bowl. The dough should be moisturized because of the longer kneading time. - For the Activated Charcoal Buns - water as needed
The dough will look loose at around 4-5 minutes before it comes together into a nice ball that’s no longer extremely sticky. - For the Activated Charcoal Buns
Transfer the dough to an oiled mixing bowl. - vegetable oil for greasing - For the Activated Charcoal Buns
For the One Proof (video)
Using a soaking wet hand, pull and round dough in a 10 & 2 motion to tuck the dough into a taut ball. - For the Activated Charcoal Buns
Cover with plastic wrap and ferment at room temperature for about an hour until roughly increased in size by 70% or even doubled. - For the Activated Charcoal Buns
Turn out the dough onto a flat work surface and aggressively punch the dough down before dividing it into 5 equal pieces and rolling into taut balls. - For the Activated Charcoal Buns

Transfer the 5 dough balls to an oiled parchment-lined rimmed baking sheet making sure not to crowd the buns. Cover and proof for 60-90 minutes. - For the Activated Charcoal Buns - vegetable oil for greasing
Bake at 400°F for 20 minutes. - For the Activated Charcoal Buns
Remove from the oven and place the buns on a wire rack. Let them cool for several hours, or until cool to the touch. - For the Activated Charcoal Buns
For the Two Proofs (Brian Lagerstrom)
https://www.brianlagerstrom.com/recipes/perfect-burger-bun
Using a soaking wet hand, pull and round dough in a 10 & 2 motion to tuck the dough into a taut ball.
Cover with plastic wrap and ferment at room temperature for about about 30 minutes
After 30 minutes the dough should have gassed up quite a bit. Aggressively punch down the dough so that you can perform a strength building fold and 10-2 rounding.
After the strength building, fold and pull another 10-2 rounding, cover the dough again and allow to ferment at room temperature for another 30 minutes.
It will have risen a lot again after the second ferment, so aggressively punch it down again.
Divide into 12 equal pieces (about 100g each).
Shape and roll each piece of dough and place onto a baking sheet lined with oiled parchment. Don’t crowd buns. I recommend using at least 2 trays.
Spritz shaped buns with water and cover with a damp towel to proof for 60-90min.
Preheat the oven to 400°F.
The buns are well proofed when they can take a poke and slowly bounce back.
Spritz the oven with 10-15 sprays of water, and bake for 18-20 min, or until the buns have an internal temperature of 195.
Remove from the oven and place the buns on a wire rack. Let them cool for several hours, or until cool to the touch.
For the Sauce
For the Butter Paste
In a small mixing bowl, add butter and the flour. Mix together with your fingertips until the flour and butter are incorporated. - 2 tbsp room temperature butter - 2 tbsp flour
For the Sauce Mixture
In a high-walled skillet over medium heat, add the red wine and reduce by half. - 2 cups red wine
Then, add stock and reduce by half. - 2 cups beef or chicken stock

When the sauce reaches a rolling boil, Add the Butter Paste and whisk vigorously to emulsify. Add salt, if needed, and sugar. Reduce to a simmer. Let the sauce thicken enough to coat the back of a spoon, whisking constantly. - Butter Paste - 2 tbsp brown sugar - 2 tsp kosher salt

Then remove it from the heat. Add the cold butter and whisk vigorously to combine. Taste and season with kosher salt, pepper and more sugar, if needed. - 8 tbsp cold butter - kosher salt to taste - freshly ground black pepper to taste - 2 tbsp brown sugar
Set aside until needed. - For the Sauce
For the Beef Tongue
Thinly slice the tongue into long, flat strips. - ½ lb beef tongue

Place in a medium mixing bowl. Add the Shaoxing wine and salt and pepper, making sure to evenly coat the strips, and marinate for 30 minutes. - ¼ cup Shaoxing wine - kosher salt to taste - freshly ground black pepper to taste
Preheat a medium skillet over medium high heat and add a drizzle of neutral oil. - neutral oil as needed
Cook the marinated tongue until deeply golden brown on both sides, about 3 minutes per side. - ½ lb beef tongue
Remove from the heat and set aside and let it rest. - Beef Tongue
For the Spam (optional)
Thinly slice the spam into long, flat strips. - Spam optional
Preheat a medium skillet over medium high heat and add a drizzle of neutral oil. - neutral oil as needed
Cook the spam on each side until deeply golden brown on both sides, about 3 minutes per side. - Spam optional
Remove from heat and set aside and let it rest. - Spam optional
For the Burgers
Preheat a pan or griddle over medium high heat. Add a drizzle of neutral oil, then season one side of the patty balls with salt. - neutral oil as needed - kosher salt to taste - Patties

Transfer one patty ball in the pan, then, placing a parchment paper on top, press flat using a turning spatula. Season with salt and freshly ground pepper, then cook for 3-4 minutes, or until deeply golden brown. - kosher salt to taste - freshly ground pepper to taste - Patties
Flip the patty and repeat on the other side. - Patties - kosher salt to taste - freshly ground pepper to taste
Top with a slice of american cheese, reduce heat, and cover until the cheese is melted. - 2 slices american cheese - Patties
Remove the patty from the pan and transfer to a cooling rack placed in a rimmed baking sheet to drain excess fat. - Patties
Repeat with each burger.
For the Assembly

Slice the baked buns in half, then add 2 slices of beef tongue or seared spam to the bottom bun, top with sauce, followed by a cheeseburger patty, drizzle with more sauce then finish with the top bun. - Beef Tongue - Spam optional - 2 slices american cheese - Patties - Activated Charcoal Buns - Sauce
Repeat with remaining burgers and serve with optional toppings like pickles, tomatoes, lettuce, etc.
